title: Surface model metadata and enforce version guardrails in public API
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Add a first-class, version-aware model metadata endpoint and publish performance profiles (limits, context, supported features) so clients can programmatically discover model capabilities and pin versions safely. This ticket defines the API schema changes, the data model, DB migrations, and the rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: New /v2/models/{model_id}/metadata endpoint returns model identifier, list of published versions, default_version, pin_policy, and an array of performance profiles with fields: max_context_tokens, recommended_batching, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, supports_streaming, output_formats

Version pinning semantics implemented on routing layer: strict pin (exact version) and semantic-compatibility pin (major+compatible minors) both supported; runtime falls back according to pin_policy when pinned version is unavailable
Existing /models/catalog endpoints remain functional for 6 weeks and are documented as deprecated in OpenAPI with clear migration guidance
DB migration adds model_profiles table and backfills profiles for active catalog models; backfill run completes within maintenance window and validated by smoke tests
SDKs (JS/Python) updated to use metadata endpoint; integration test matrix passes across pinned behaviors
Telemetry emits profile_published, pin_mismatch, and pin_fallback events with tags model_id, requested_version, served_version, and profile_version
work_items: API design: openapi spec for /v2/models/{model_id}/metadata and /v2/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/profile
DB migration: create model_profiles (model_id, version, profile_json_v1, published_at, profile_version)
Catalog service: expose publish API for profile authors and validate schema
Routing: consult model metadata cache before routing; implement pin_policy enforcement and fallback logic
SDK changes: surface recommended_context and supports_streaming flags to callers
Docs: migration guide and example client usage for pinning strategies
QA: unit tests for schema validation, e2e canary with rollback hooks
Telemetry: add metrics and dashboards for profile adoption and fallback rates
notes: Design constraints: maintain strictly additive schema changes so older SDKs get best-effort behavior rather than hard failures.

Profile schema v1 restricts field types to primitives (numbers/strings/booleans) to avoid complex nested objects; any future richer metadata must use a namespaced key to preserve flat JSON in our catalog DB.
Pinning modes considered: strict, semver-compatible, rolling-default. We will ship strict and semver-compatible initially; rolling-default deferred.
We must rate-limit metadata endpoint to prevent misuse; per-tenant cache TTL recommended 5 minutes with ETag support for conditional GETs.
Edge case: private/on-prem customers may manage profiles offline; ensure metadata endpoint supports 'managed_by' flag and 'external_profile_url' for manual ingestion.
